title: Increased evolutionary rate in the Z-chromosome of Morpho butterflies and implications for speciation
authors: Villavicencio ML; Ledamoisel J; Lopez-Roques C; Debat V; Llaurens V
one_liner_zh: 该文研究蝴蝶Z染色体进化与物种形成，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The evolution of reproductive isolation between populations shapes divergence in genome structure and content: comparing the genomes of closely-related species can thus enlighten the speciation process. Comparisons of genomes of allopatric vs . sympatric species sharing similar vs . dissimilar ecological niches allows to specifically investigate the effect of reinforcement and ecological specialization on genome evolution. In the butterfly genus Morpho , several species can be found in sympatry presenting specialisation in different microhabitats and temporal niches. Here, we sequenced, assembled and annotated the genomes of 8 Morpho species and used previously published genomes of three other Morpho species to study genomic rearrangements and signatures of positive selection. We found extensive chromosomal rearrangements in the Z chromosome compared to the autosomes, particularly among closely related sympatric species occupying similar niches, pointing at the putative role of inversions in preventing gene flow at a postzygotic level. We also detected a higher proportion of genes under positive selection on the Z-chromosome compared to the autosomes, suggesting a potential role of the Z-chromosome in driving adaptive evolution in Morpho . Finally, because of the divergence in daily activities between species, we studied the evolution of eight genes involved in the circadian clock and detected a signature of positive selection on the gene Period , located in the Z chromosome. By studying the evolution of genome structure and coding sequences, our study indicates fast evolution of the Z-chromosome, partly driven by selection, throughout this genus, highlighting the putative implication of this sexual chromosome on pre and post-zygotic isolation.
abstract_zh: 生殖隔离的演化塑造了基因组结构与内容的差异：因此，比较近缘物种的基因组可以揭示物种形成过程。比较同域与异域分布、生态位相似与不相似的物种基因组，可以专门研究强化作用和生态特化对基因组演化的影响。在闪蝶属（Morpho）中，多个物种可同域共存，并表现出对不同微栖息地和时间生态位的特化。本研究对8种闪蝶属物种的基因组进行了测序、组装和注释，并利用已发表的另外3种闪蝶属物种的基因组，研究了基因组重排和正选择信号。我们发现，与常染色体相比，Z染色体上存在广泛的染色体重排，尤其是在占据相似生态位的近缘同域物种中，这提示倒位可能在合子后水平上阻止基因流方面发挥潜在作用。我们还检测到Z染色体上受正选择的基因比例高于常染色体，表明Z染色体可能在驱动闪蝶属适应性演化中发挥潜在作用。最后，鉴于物种间日常活动时间的差异，我们研究了参与昼夜节律时钟的八个基因的演化，并在位于Z染色体上的Period基因中检测到正选择信号。通过研究基因组结构和编码序列的演化，我们的研究表明，在整个属中，Z染色体演化迅速，部分由选择驱动，突显了这条性染色体在合子前和合子后隔离中的潜在作用。
